source.title: Process Piping - ASME Code for Pressure Piping, B31
source.note: Technical content only. Publisher front/back matter, running heads, printed folios and edition change markers are omitted. Values are as printed; the ASME ellipsis (no value / not permitted) is represented as null.

paragraphs.text: This Appendix covers pressure–temperature ratings, materials, dimensions, and marking of forged aluminum alloy flanges, as an alternative to applying the rules in paras. 304.5.1(b) and 304.5.2(b). DN 15 (NPS 1∕2) through DN 600 (NPS 24) flanges may be welding neck, slip-on, socket welding, lapped, or blind in ratings of Classes 150, 300, and 600.
Requirements and recommendations regarding bolting and gaskets are included.

Ratings are maximum allowable working gage pressures at the temperatures shown in Table L301.1-1 (Table L301.1-1C) and L301.2U for the applicable material and pressure Class. For intermediate temperatures, linear interpolation is permitted.

(a) In addition to the considerations in para. F312.1, consideration shall be given to the low modulus of elasticity of aluminum alloys. External moments should be limited, and controlled bolt tightening or other techniques may be necessary to achieve and maintain a leak-free joint.
(b) For ratings of slip-on and socket welding flanges made of Alloy 6061-T6, see Table L301.1-1 (Table L301.1-1C).

Application of the ratings in this Appendix to flanged joints at both high and low temperatures shall take into consideration the risk of leakage due to forces and moments developed in the connected piping or equipment. The following provisions are intended to minimize these risks.
welding flanges are not recommended for service below −50°F if flanges are subject to thermal cycling.

Conductivity. Because aluminum alloys have thermal expansion coefficients approximately twice those for steel, and thermal conductivity approximately three times that of steel, it may be necessary to provide for differential expansion and expansion rates between components of the flanged joint. Consideration shall be given to thermal transients (e.g., startup, shutdown, and upset) in addition to the operating temperature of the joint.
A flange shall be capable of withstanding a hydrostatic test at 1.5 times its 100°F pressure rating.
Marking shall be in accordance with MSS SP-25, except as follows. Marking shall be stamped on the edge of each flange.
The manufacturer’s name or trademark shall be applied.
The marking ASTM B247 shall be applied, followed by the applicable alloy and temper designations.
The marking shall be the applicable rating Class — 150, 300, or 600.
The marking B31.3L shall be applied.

The marking of NPS shall be applied. A reducing size shall be designated by its two nominal pipe sizes. See examples in Note (4) of Table 6, ASME B16.5. GENERAL NOTE: Pressures are in kPa; temperatures are in °C. NOTES: (1) The minimum temperature is −269°C. The maximum rating below 38°C shall be the rating shown for 38°C. (2) Ratings apply to welding neck, lapped, and blind flanges. (3) Ratings apply to slip-on and socket welding flanges.
Flanges shall be forgings conforming to ASTM B247. For specific alloys and tempers, see Table L301.1-1 (Table L301.1-1C). For precautions in use, see para. 323.5 and Appendix F, para. F323.

sections.heading: Repair Welding of Flanges. Repair welding of

paragraphs.text: flanges manufactured to this Appendix shall be restricted to any damaged areas of the weld bevel of welding neck flanges unless specifically approved by the Purchaser after consideration of the extent, location, and effect on temper and ductility. Repair welding of any area other than the weld bevel on 6061-T6 welding neck flanges shall restrict the pressure/temperature ratings to those specified for slip-on and socket welding flanges in Table L301.1-1 (Table L301.1-1C). Any repair welding shall be performed in accordance with para. 328.6. GENERAL NOTE: Pressures are in psig; temperatures are in °F. NOTES: (1) The minimum temperature is −452°F. The maximum rating below 100°F shall be the rating shown for 100°F. (2) Ratings apply to welding neck, lapped, and blind flanges. (3) Ratings apply to slip-on and socket welding flanges.
Bolting listed in Table L303.2-1 and in ASME B16.5, Table 1B, may be used subject to the following limitations.
listed as high strength in ASME B16.5, Table 1B, may be used in any flanged joints. See para. L305.
materials in Table L303.2-1, and bolting listed as intermediate strength in ASME B16.5, Table 1B, may be used in any flanged joints. See para. L305.
listed as low strength in ASME B16.5, Table 1B, may be used in Classes 150 and 300 flanged joints. See para. L305.
Gaskets listed in ASME B16.5, Nonmandatory Appendix B, Table B-1, Group Ia may be used with any rating Class and bolting. GENERAL NOTE Repair welding of bolting material is prohibited.

sections.heading: Gaskets for Low-Strength Bolting. If bolting

paragraphs.text: listed as low strength (see para. L303.2.3) is used, gaskets listed in ASME B16.5, Nonmandatory Appendix B, Table B1, Group Ia shall be used.

sections.heading: Gaskets for Class 150 Flanged Joints. It is

paragraphs.text: recommended that only gaskets listed in ASME B16.5, Nonmandatory Appendix B, Table B-1, Group Ia be used.

sections.heading: Gaskets for Class 300 and Higher Flanged

paragraphs.text: Joints. It is recommended that only gaskets listed in ASME B16.5, Nonmandatory Appendix B, Table B-1, Group I be used. For gaskets in Group Ib, line flanges should be of the welding neck or lapped joint type; controlled-torque tightening practices should be used.
(a) Flanges shall meet the dimensional and tolerance requirements of ASME B16.5.
(b) Flange facing and facing finish shall be in accordance with ASME B16.5, except that small male and female facings (on ends of pipe) shall not be used.
The following design considerations are applicable to all flanged joints that incorporate a flange manufactured to this Appendix:
(a) The differential expansion within a flanged joint shall be considered; also, see para. F312.

(b) Where a gasket other than those recommended in para. L303.3 is specified, the designer shall verify by calculations the ability of the selected bolting to seat the selected gasket and maintain a sealed joint under the expected operating conditions without over-stressing the components.
